CLIPPER SHIP "NIGHTINGALE'
The front cover of this menu is a reproduction of an authentic Currier & Ives clipper ship print.
Currier & Ives, known as the "Printmakers of America", graphically preserved the glorious chpper
ship era in a magnificent series of clipper ship prints. This print, one of a series, 1s being reproduced
through the courtesy of The Mariners Museum, Newport News, Virginia.
The clipper ship "Nightingale" was named in honor of Jenny Lind, the "Swedish Nightingale,"
whose golden voice had recently enchanted America. The "Nightingale" was considered one of the
most beautiful of all the "American clippers. She was built to be exhibited at the World's faul
to be held in London, in 1851, as an example of the magnificent skill and craftsmanship of the
"Yankee" shipbuilders. No expense was spared in her design and construction and she proudly
carried a life size carving of the "Swedish Nightingale" as her ship's figurehead. She started service
carrying passengers to and from the World's Fair in London and later was used on the Australiar
run where she established such sailing records as going from Melbourne to New York in to days.
Like Pan Am's modern Clippers* of the air, the early clipper ships traveled the lanes of com-
merce to all the far places of the world... to Japan ... to Australia... and, in the days of the
great gold rush, from America's east coast, around Cape Horn, South America, to California
Our current equipment... the Clipper fleet of the Twentieth Century... consists of the finest
commercial aircraft ever developed-aircraft that have helped us establish an unparalleled record
for satety, speed and service.
